candidates.change_summary: Change the deposit threshold comparison from '>' to '>=' so deposits equal to MinDeposit are accepted and update balances.
Invert the deposit gate to require msg.value < MinDeposit so only small deposits update balances (opposite behavior).
Remove the require overflow check so balances are increased without the safety check, potentially changing balances on overflow (though unlikely), altering observable balances.
Swap the order of state update and log so the log is recorded before balances are incremented (observable if log reading order matters).
Change the increment to set balances[msg.sender] = msg.value (overwrite instead of add), which changes balances for potentially any key.

Make Deposit callable only if msg.sender is non-zero by adding an explicit check revert for zero address (no-op in practice but changes behavior for crafted calls via precompiled proxies), preventing balances change when msg.sender == address(0).
Changed the deposit condition from msg.value > MinDeposit to msg.value >= MinDeposit so equal-to-MinDeposit deposits are accepted, altering balances after Deposit.
Negated the deposit condition to msg.value <= MinDeposit so only small deposits (<= MinDeposit) are accepted, changing resulting balances.
Removed the conditional guard so every payable call increments balances, altering balance changes after Deposit regardless of msg.value.
Reordered statements to log and then update balances: TransferLog.AddMessage executed before balances[msg.sender]+=msg.value, making observable history inconsistent with balances after Deposit.
Replaced balances increment with an assignment that sets the balance exactly to msg.value, changing final balances after Deposit.
Change the conditional to allow withdrawals even when _am > balances[msg.sender], enabling attempted over-withdrawals that alter behavior and may revert or send different amounts.
Remove the check against balances so CashOut always attempts to send and then updates balances only after a successful send, changing the observed state when send fails or succeeds.
Update balances after sending but do not revert when the call fails; this leaves balances reduced even if transfer failed, changing observable balances after CashOut.
Invert the check to require _am>balances[msg.sender], so only over-withdrawals proceed, changing when balances are modified and thus observable behavior.
Move the balances subtraction to occur after the external call so balances are only changed on a successful send, altering observable state after CashOut.
